questions.prompt: What does Stone do after seeing Burrow stranded across the stream?
choices: Stone steps onto the rope bridge.
Stone waits for Pip to cross first.
questions.answer: Stone steps onto the rope bridge.
questions.evidenceText: Stone stepped onto the bridge. It creaked under Stone's weight. Stone kept going.

questions.prompt: Why does Stone face the bridge even though Stone is afraid?
choices: Pip has hidden a prize across the stream.
The bridge is about to drift downstream.
questions.evidenceText: "Help!" called Burrow. "I cannot find the tunnel. Everything looks the same to me!"

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: Stone would not cross the bridge. "There is a troll under the bridge," said Stone. "I do not want to meet it."
Stone stepped onto the bridge. It creaked under Stone's weight. Stone kept going.

questions.rationale: Stone says he does not want to cross the bridge, but when Burrow cannot find the tunnel, Stone steps onto the bridge and keeps going; helping Burrow motivates Stone to face the bridge despite being afraid.

questions.prompt: What lesson does Stone's careful return across the bridge show?
choices: A frightening task can be managed one step at a time.
Looking ahead made the bridge stop moving under Stone.
Walking with Burrow removed all of Stone's fear.
questions.answer: A frightening task can be managed one step at a time.
questions.rationale: Stone steps onto the creaking bridge and later crosses by looking at the far end, one step then another; this shows a frightening task can be managed one step at a time.
questions.evidenceText: Stone did not look at the water. Stone looked at the far end of the bridge. One step, then another.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: Stone stepped onto the bridge. It creaked under Stone's weight. Stone kept going.
